column2: Interactions with ArgR regulation can lead to no Arg production with low ppGpp

As of 11/10/26, could not find strong evidence that ppGpp induces relA transcription. relA expression changed -0.36 log2 during isoleucine starvation with native RelA (Traxler et al. 2008 Mol Microbiol, Table S2). relA also was not listed among genes changing at least 2.8-fold (log2 ratio 1.5, for genes with an average log2 signal above 9) during the SHX stringent response (Durfee et al. 2008 J Bacteriol), which might suggest little change too (but could also mean low signal or there maybe there was some other reason it was not quantified). Also, downstream mazE/mazF on the same operon changed only a little +0.06/+0.25 log2 (Sanchez-Vazquez et al. 2019, category E). The curated activation used the average activator fold change since there was no value for relA, which made relA expression about 27x higher when ppGpp-bound and created an unsupported ppGpp -> RelA -> ppGpp loop. As of 11/21/26, EcoCyc cites Goodman 2012 (Nat Chem Biol research highlight of Shyp et al. 2012, EMBO Rep) for this regulation, which reports ppGpp allosterically activating RelA enzyme activity (raising kcat), not relA transcription. relA appears in Traxler et al. 2008 Table S2 because it is deleted in the relA and relA spoT strains (-3.8 and -4.1 log2 vs the unstarved wild type), and as mentioned already, it changed -0.36 log2, so the table does not imply activation. The 2015 RNA-seq used by the ParCa has relA at 95.9 TPM in M9 glucose both with and without amino acids, while the model's target ppGpp differs about 2.4-fold between them (49 vs 21 uM, but note that ppGpp was not actually measured with that experiment). With all of this combined (the model's RNA-seq showing virtually no change in relA expression between conditions assumed to have different ppGpp concentrations, Traxler et al. 2008 showing little to no change, and if anything a small decrease, and Goodman 2012 indicating that ppGpp activates RelA enzyme activity rather than relA transcription), it is likely safe to remove the ppGpp -> relA regulation for now and avoid the nearly 27x induction.
